title: One-horse carriage, two-horse carriage
paragraphs: “I hear there’s way too much exploitation at Takt.”
“I get that he wants to save up, though…”

Well, he is a reincarnated person, after all. I guess that penny-pinching mentality is just ingrained in him. It’s kind of like one of those exploitative companies that don’t pass on their profits to employees, even when they make a ton of money.
“Money, you see, doesn’t do you any good if you just hoard it. Isn’t it all about spending it in a way that benefits you?”

said Panda. He’s got a point. I, too, have earned a lot and reinvested it in Lady Filolial, her ranch, the land, the races, and Filo-chan merchandise. You could certainly call that a truly meaningful way to spend it. Even Father, as I remember him, was smiling.
“And you’re the one saying that, Rasa-san?”
“I don’t really like money, you know. But it’s fine as long as you have a good use for it. If you just hoard it needlessly, isn’t all that’s left in the end just a messy, messy fight?”

Come to think of it, Panda is very attached to money, but I don’t really know how he spends it. I see him using it for drinks and meals that day, but even when his equipment and such are covered, he still seems to be saving it up. I have a vivid memory of him traveling as a merchant with Keel.
“What’s the matter? You’ve been staring at me for a while now.”
“I just can’t seem to remember where you spend your money.”
“It’s obviously on mercenaries for that day’s earnings, isn’t it? At most, I blow it all on gear, food and drink, or supporting my subordinates.”
“No… I seem to recall you were always a bit short on cash, even though you were making more than that…”
“Oh, come to think of it, the Spear Hero said he knew the ‘me’ from another world, didn’t he?”
The panda therianthrope furrows his brow as he looks at me.
“So that’s why Lasa is so obsessed with money…”
Father stares intently at the panda therianthrope.
“It’s a cliché, but maybe a family member has a serious illness and needs money or something?”
“Nope.”
“That’s too similar to another character’s backstory.”
That’s the tiger siblings’ story. I’m not saying something like that couldn’t happen, but it’s not exactly exciting.

“Motoyasu-kun let slip something that’s really got me curious, but I’ll put that on hold for now. If it’s a family issue, Siltvelt would probably cover it… So maybe he’s sending money back to his hometown village… or donating to an orphanage?”
“Oh, do I really look like I’m capable of something like that?”
“That’s a reaction that’s got me a little curious. From what I’ve heard, Ms. Rasa is apparently a rare species even in Siltvelt.”
Ah, come to think of it, the folks in Siltvelt did mention that. I suppose pandas are considered rare creatures in this world, too.

But… what can I say about Father? He seems to spend a lot of time interacting with therianthropes and monsters whose eyes are either slightly dark or, conversely, white. Your Older Sister is one example, the panda therianthrope is another… and you, too. I wish he’d share just a little more of that curiosity with the Filolials.

Oh? I feel like the Older Sister from my memories is protesting… but before she can step forward, a creature modeled after her is making its presence known. It’s striking a pose just like a Rider transforming. Well, I suppose there’s no need to worry about it. I’ll wave my hand to clear my mind.
“It doesn’t matter that I’m a miser. I mean, what about you Filolials—the Spear Heroes?”
“Such a base desire as greed for money does not exist among the Filolials.”
They’re all kind and earnest little ones. They each have their own hobbies and preferences, but they’re not tainted by greed. That’s right… except for their appetite!
“The other day, I saw the Filolials playing in the castle treasury with their eyes all sparkling.”
“They were just playing because they were drawn to shiny things. They collect everything—whether it’s broken glass or a snapped sword!　In fact, they absolutely love carriages!”
“That’s just like a bird… so they don’t understand the value of money, do they? Though I’m not really sure about the carriages.”
“When Father said he’d give them their own personal carriages as a reward, the Filolials rushed headlong to complete the tasks assigned to them! It’s truly wonderful!”
“I seriously can’t wrap my head around that way of thinking, you know?”
Ugh… Back then, Father probably hadn’t quite caught up with understanding Filolial yet. But given his abilities, I’m sure he’ll get used to it in no time.
“Yuki-chan and the others feel the same way, don’t they?”
“Of course. A private carriage is a dream, isn’t it?”
“Yeah.”
“I want one!”
“So this is a shared sentiment… Is it like the feeling of ‘a man’s castle’—a home of one’s own?”
“By the way, Filo-tan also received a metal carriage from Father and was happily polishing it.”

That was around the time we went to Carmilla Island. That was before she started getting seasick. Since Filo-tan was on the same ship, I went to see her and happened to catch her happily polishing her carriage. As luck would have it, Father and the others weren’t around, so—foolish as I am—I seized the opportunity to approach Filo-tan and perform a “carriage slam” instead of a “wall slam.”
“Hey, what are you doing here? Is Naofumi making you do hard labor again?”
“Ah! Filo’s carriage is getting dirty!”
The next moment, I was kicked and slammed into the Wall.
“Guh!?”
“Filo’s doing this because she wants to!”

Saying that, Filo-tan carefully wiped down the spot where I’d touched her. After that, I staggered away, figuring that if she was doing it willingly, there was nothing I could do—I’d just ended up making her angry. If I were to dirty Filo-tan… I mean, Lady Filolial’s carriage any further, I’d surely end up being hated by her.
“I understand it’s just her nature… but so a carriage is the best way to thank Sakura-chan and the others, is it?”
“That’s right! Of course, a carriage studded with rare ores and gems would make them even happier.”
“Is that so?”
And with that, Father asked everyone.
“Hmm? I don’t want a rickety one.”
“A flashy one is fine, but I don’t like tacky decorations.”
“The fancier, the better!”
In other words, there are all sorts of preferences, aren’t there?

“You’ve got the general idea right. But what kind of sensibility is this—being able to tell the difference between carriages when you don’t even understand the value of money? They might get it if we compared carriages to currency… but I really don’t want to have to manage things in units like ‘one carriage’ or ‘two carriages.’”
“That’s a brilliant idea.”
“It’s not a great idea. It’d be way more of a hassle than stone money.”
“Then let’s have wooden carriages, iron carriages, and silver carriages! What do you think?”
“Just don’t make them into units like copper, silver, and gold coins, okay? I don’t want the quality of my orders to change depending on which carriage I’m given.”

I think this would be a good deal with Filolial, but if Father disapproves, let’s use it for secret transactions. It’d also be a good idea to come up with some custom parts. Just like the tires we made in the last loop specifically for Second Mode, developing parts for carriages looks like it’ll be a challenge for us going forward.
“It’s kind of like explaining Filolial’s ecology while subtly keeping the conversation on the topic of money… Larsa, you’d better think this through.”
“Is this going to be my fault?”
“You’re the one who asked the Filolials about money, Larsa.”
“Well, I guess so. I suppose it’s weird to ask monsters about money, huh?”
“Eating, playing, and sleeping are the basics, after all. Appetite is more important, right?”
“I like eating and drinking, too.”
“I’m curious where the money Larsa earns goes… but maybe we can save that for another time.”
“Curiosity leads to ruin, you know? Shield Hero?”
It seems the panda is trying to threaten Father, but he’s already ignoring what the panda is saying. Father is really good at gauging these kinds of boundaries.
“It’s typical of the panda—he’s probably saving up for cute merchandise and clothes.”

In the first world, the panda was involved in the gathering of all sorts of outfits and such in exactly that way. Don’t you dare underestimate my powers of observation. If you want, I could even expose every single one of your secrets!
“I-t-t-o-t-a-l-l-y! Stop adding weird elements to my character!”

“Hahaha… Either way, we’re heading to the country of Shieldfreeden, which used to be part of the Takt faction. We’ll have to check out the situation over there. Plus, we need to find a safe hideout for the survivors.”
“You sure changed the subject abruptly… Whatever, I guess. I just hope this doesn’t turn into a hassle.”
“Exactly!”
And so, the plane carrying us flew off toward Shieldfreeden, where dark clouds loomed. Whoosh, as they say.
After a while, our flight continued, and we landed at the airfield in Shieldfreeden, our destination. Father is looking out the airplane window.
“It feels more like a military base than an airport, doesn’t it?”

I followed Father’s lead and looked out the window too. The view was reminiscent of a run-down airstrip in some remote corner of a free country. We’d already destroyed most of the aircraft Takt had prepared, so there weren’t many left. It looked like airships and the like could take off and land here as well. All sorts of equipment is stacked here, and a bit further away, there’s a barbed-wire fence set up.
“Just looking at this place, it makes it feel a little less like we’ve come to another world.”
“That’s true.”

Looking beyond the barbed wire… there’s a group of people waving flags and shouting—perhaps to welcome us to their country. That’s quite a commendable gesture. They should be praising and honoring Father even more.
“Are they welcoming us over there? It’s hard to tell from this far away.”
“This is my chance to shine, Motoyasu Ai! Mmm!”

I squint as hard as I can and glare at the crowd in front of the chain-link fence. …It does seem like they’re welcoming us. But why are their cheeks twitching a bit? This is the arrival of Father, who showed mercy to you self-righteous fools. To claim dissatisfaction despite that is the height of foolishness, isn’t it? Behind them, I can see people being led away, bound with ropes.
“It seems they are welcoming us. For some reason, the people in the back are tied up.”
As we stood there scratching our heads, a staff member from Shieldfreeden entered the plane and began talking with one of our staff members.
“Um… apparently, a dissident group had infiltrated the organization welcoming the Shield Hero and attempted to unfurl a banner containing slanderous remarks.”
“They’re the kind of people like the Three Heroes Church, aren’t they?”

By the way, the Three Heroes Church has already been designated a cult. Not only did Itsuki die, but the state religion of Melromarc has already changed on the grounds that they used the nation’s soldiers for personal gain.

That’s thanks to the Queen slipping back into the country amid the chaos. Of course, the hunting of Demi-Human slaves has been banned, those involved have been punished, and the slaves are reportedly being protected. That’s where Éclair’s hard work comes in.
“Does that just mean the Takt faction is deeply entrenched?”
“I hear the citizens, now that they know the truth, are gathering to welcome the Shield Hero.”
“It doesn’t look that way to me, though.”
“Their faces are all tense… Aren’t they just terrified of what kind of unreasonable demands or heavy taxes might be imposed on them?”
“Well… I suppose that’s just how inspections by the victorious nation go. I wonder if that Commissioner came to this country feeling the same way…”
It seems we’re ready to disembark—the staff are guiding us off the plane.
“I guess the time between getting off the plane and entering the building is the perfect opportunity?”

“What?”—that’s a question neither Father nor I need to ask. It’s about how to deal with the attacks the Takt faction is likely to launch. Father and I have analyzed that those kinds of underhanded scoundrels will undoubtedly make a move.

Our allies on the Shieldfreeden side are also on high alert, trying to thwart them in advance, but there’s no end to the number of those kinds of people. Even after the world achieved peace, there were still as many people as there are stars in the sky who were out to kill Father. After all, they’re the kind of people who plot to eliminate a hero who gets in their way. Of course, Father and I made sure those scoundrels got what they deserved. HAHAHA.
“Actually, don’t you think we should keep an eye out for those kinds of guys scheming behind the scenes for a while?”
“You’re right.”
“Want me to act as your shield? That’s what I was hired for, after all.”
“What kind of hero do you think I am? Lasa, it’d actually be a big help if you could focus on protecting everyone else around me instead.”

At Father’s reply, Panda shrugged and let out a light sigh. Personally, I’m incredibly anxious at the thought of Father facing even the slightest danger, but it’s an undeniable fact that his defensive abilities are top-notch.
“That’s true. Still, is there really anyone on your team who can’t handle this kind of attack?”
“Hmm?”
“The atmosphere feels a bit tense.”
“Some lowly wretches are trying to satisfy their own selfish desires. I won’t show them any openings.”

Yuki-chan and the others understand as well. As for Sakura-chan… she still looks sleepy. …I really do think this over and over again, but I just can’t believe that, depending on how she’s raised, Sakura-chan could turn into Filo-tan.

It’s precisely because I’ve experienced it firsthand that this contrast strikes me as so strange. Still… you’re right. Sakura-chan really did look a lot like Filo-tan when she was basking in the warm sunlight.
